events.summary: iOS 6.1 Beta 1 is represented by 5 selected source-linked change records from the 2012-11-01 milestone; unsupported routes and build guesses remain excluded.

blocks.text: Release identity and boundary

Contemporaneous coverage places the first iOS 6.1 developer seed on November 1, 2012. Earlier 6.0.1 reporting describes carrier testing rather than a developer distribution, so this archive does not invent a 6.0.1 beta route.

citations.locator: Release date — Thursday November 1, 2012
6.0.1 boundary — Apple has begun carrier testing of iOS 6.0.1

blocks.text: Selected milestone record

The selected records cover the new local-search interface, boarding-pass relevance, advertising-identifier reset, a reported Siri ticket workflow, and an iCloud plan-change restriction later attributed specifically to this first seed.

changes.title: iCloud storage-plan changes
changes.canonicalSummary: The first two 6.1 seeds blocked iCloud storage-plan upgrades and downgrades; Beta 3 marked that restriction as repaired.

changes.verificationMethod: The retained Beta 2 article reproduces developer-note language that explicitly labels the restriction as Beta 1 state.

changes.title: Phone passcode bypass
changes.canonicalSummary: Improved emergency-call lock-state handling closed a path that could bypass the passcode and expose the Phone app.
changes.summary: Apple-attributed notes said the seed repaired the reported passcode bug, a lock-screen sequence that exposed Phone access without authentication.
changes.verificationMethod: Two contemporaneous reports independently identify the Apple-attributed fix and the same beta route.

changes.title: Evasi0n jailbreak path
changes.canonicalSummary: The first seed still allowed evasi0n to run; the relabeled second seed changed that state by patching at least its time-zone-settings exploit.
changes.summary: A researcher testing Beta 2 found that Apple had patched at least the time-zone flaw used by evasi0n.
changes.verificationMethod: Two contemporaneous reports quote the same named researcher; they support the tested time-zone change but not a claim that every jailbreak path was closed.
